record.paper_title: Recent results and open problems on parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities
record.context_brief: Existence of global grow-up for all infinite-inradius domains
record.original_question: Assume q ≥ p and let Ω be an unbounded domain whose inradius ρ(Ω) = sup_{x∈Ω} dist(x,∂Ω) is infinite. Theorem 3.1(ii) shows that some initial data then produce solutions that become unbounded, but this unboundedness may occur either in finite time or only as t → ∞. Theorem 3.5 gives genuine unbounded global solutions when Ω contains a cone. Does there exist an unbounded global solution for every domain with ρ(Ω)=∞ whenever q ≥ p?

Open problem 7. Does there exist unbounded global solutions whenever ρ(Ω) = ∞ and q ≥ p ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p>1$ and $q>1$ with $q\ge p$. For an unbounded smooth domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, define the inradius
$$\rho(\Omega)=\sup_{x\in\Omega}\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)=\sup\{r>0:\Omega \text{ contains a ball of radius } r\}.$$
Consider the semilinear parabolic Dirichlet problem
$$
\begin{cases}
u_t-\Delta u = u^{p}+|\nabla u|^{q}, & x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\
u(x,t)=0, & x\in\partial\Omega,\ t>0,\\
u(x,0)=\varphi(x)\ge 0, & x\in\Omega,
\end{cases}
$$
with nonnegative initial data $\varphi\in L^\infty(\Omega)\cap C(\overline\Omega)$ vanishing on $\partial\Omega$. Let $u$ denote the maximal classical nonnegative solution defined on $[0,T^*)$, with $T^*\in(0,\infty]$ the maximal existence time. Call $u$ an "unbounded global solution" if $T^*=\infty$ and $\lim_{t\to\infty}\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}=\infty$.

Question: Assuming $\rho(\Omega)=\infty$ and $q\ge p$, does there always exist an initial datum $\varphi$ for which the corresponding solution is an unbounded global solution (rather than blowing up in finite time)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is presented as an open problem in a recent survey on parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities. Web searches did not turn up any subsequent work resolving the existence of unbounded global solutions for arbitrary unbounded domains with infinite inradius when q ≥ p; only partial results (e.g., for domains containing a cone) appear in the literature.
